bib.title: Seq2SQL: Generating Structured Queries from Natural Language using Reinforcement Learning

question: Can natural language questions be translated to SQL queries over unseen table schemas by exploiting SQL structure and execution-based RL rewards?
hypothesis: WHERE conditions are unordered, so cross entropy wrongly penalises equivalent queries; optimising execution correctness with policy gradient should do better.
contributions: Seq2SQL, a network that uses SQL structure to prune the output space and policy-based RL with in-the-loop execution for the WHERE clause
WikiSQL, 80654 hand-annotated question/SQL/table examples over 24241 tables, plus a query execution engine

method.summary: Seq2SQL has an aggregation classifier, a SELECT column pointer and a WHERE pointer decoder. The first two use cross entropy; WHERE is first trained with teacher forcing, then with REINFORCE using a reward from executing the generated query. Compared with a Dong & Lapata seq2seq baseline and an augmented pointer network on WikiSQL.
method.task: natural language to SQL (single-table semantic parsing)

datasets.name: WikiSQL
datasets.split: random train/dev/test, each table in exactly one split; split sizes not stated
datasets.source: Crowdsourced on Amazon Mechanical Turk from Wikipedia tables (Bhagavatula et al. 2013); licence not stated
datasets.preprocessing: Stanford CoreNLP tokenisation; normalised tokens for training, reverted to original gloss before output so queries execute. Tables filtered: ragged rows, cells over 50 chars, empty header, under 5 rows or 5 columns, over 40% identical cells in a row; last row dropped. 6 random SQL queries per table, non-empty results only; paraphrase kept if at least one verifier approved and edit distance over 10.

models.name: Seq2SQL
models.architecture: 2-layer bidirectional LSTM encoder, aggregation classifier, SELECT column pointer, 2-layer unidirectional LSTM pointer decoder for WHERE
models.init_from: inferred: trained from scratch with fixed GloVe + character n-gram embeddings; RL stage continues from teacher-forced version

other.embeddings: fixed GloVe plus character n-gram embeddings (Hashimoto et al. 2016)

models.name: Seq2SQL (no RL)
models.architecture: same as Seq2SQL, WHERE supervised by teacher forcing

models.name: Aug Ptr Network
models.architecture: pointer network over columns + question + SQL vocabulary, 2-layer bi-LSTM encoder, 2-layer LSTM decoder

models.name: Baseline (Dong & Lapata 2016)
models.architecture: attentional seq2seq, OpenNMT variant with global attention and input feeding, same 2-layer bi-LSTM encoder

training.objective: L = L_agg + L_sel + L_whe, equally weighted; CE for aggregation and SELECT, policy gradient (single Monte-Carlo sample) on reward -2 invalid SQL, -1 valid but wrong result, +1 correct result for WHERE
training.epochs: maximum 300, early stopping on dev execution accuracy

other.rl_schedule: first train with WHERE teacher-forced, then continue with RL; RL epochs not stated

inference.decoding: argmax over pointer scores (Seq2SQL); beam size 5 with unknown-word replacement by highest-attention input word for the Dong & Lapata baseline
inference.samples: during RL training the next token is sampled from the output distribution; one sample per example

metrics.name: Execution accuracy (Acc_ex)
metrics.definition: N_ex/N: share of queries that execute to the correct result

metrics.name: Logical form accuracy (Acc_lf)
metrics.definition: N_lf/N: share of queries with exact string match to the ground truth query

eval.protocol: single reported number per model on dev and test; no seeds or significance tests

limits: Execution accuracy can credit a query that does not match the question but returns the same result; logical form accuracy penalises correct queries with reordered conditions (3.1).
Only single-table queries with an aggregation, one SELECT column and AND-joined conditions; the generator uses only =, > and < (Appendix A).
One run per model, no seeds, variance or significance tests; learning rate, batch size and RL epochs not given.
Table content is not used by the model, only column names and the question.
Dataset questions are paraphrases of template-generated questions, so they may be less varied than natural user questions (inferred, not conceded).

terms.definition: Acc_ex = N_ex/N, queries that execute to the correct result
Acc_lf = N_lf/N, queries with exact string match to the ground truth query

code.snippet: R(q(y), qg) = -2 if q(y) is not a valid SQL query; -1 if valid and executes to an incorrect result; +1 if valid and executes to the correct result
